name: The Path of the Adept
summary: The Path of the Adept is a trial of passage assigned by Knight-Lord Bloodvalor in Silvermoon City to rising Blood Knights. Initiates must scour perilous dungeons and Scourge-held territories across Azeroth to secure materials for crafting their signature polearm and recover the insignia of a fallen comrade. Completing this arduous journey marks a paladin's true ascension within the ranks of the Blood Knights.

sections.title: A Rite of Blood and Steel
sections.body: Before any initiate can be formally recognized as an adept of the Blood Knights, they are required to gather the exotic components necessary to forge their order's signature weapon: the blood-tempered ranseur. Knight-Lord Bloodvalor tasks aspiring knights with proving their resolve through an arduous trek spanning distant lands, testing their combat prowess against dark sorcery, monstrous cultists, and ravenous beasts.

sections.title: Inheriting the Insignia
sections.body: Rank and recognition within the Blood Knights are not merely bestowed; they are inherited from those who fell in service to Quel'Thalas. Because only a finite number of official insignia were minted when the order was founded, every rising adept must claim an insignia from a deceased predecessor. Candidates must journey into the blighted Scourge stronghold of Deatholme to recover the emblem of Blood Knight Dawnstar, who fell leading an assault near the Tower of the Damned.

sections.title: Trials Across Azeroth
sections.body: The physical materials required for the ranseur take the adept deep into hostile territories. Bloodvalor's ledger directs them to the naga haunting the ruins outside Blackfathom Deeps for a Corrupted Kor Gem, into the burning depths of Orgrimmar's Ragefire Chasm to extract the Blood of the Wrathful, and into the courtyard of Shadowfang Keep to retrieve Bloodforged Ingots hidden away near the stables.

faq.q: What is the purpose of The Path of the Adept?
aliases: why do path of the adept
faq.answer: It serves as the formal rite of passage for Blood Knight initiates seeking the rank of adept. Initiates must gather rare materials to forge their blood-tempered ranseur and recover an insignia from a fallen knight.
Knight-Lord Bloodvalor, a senior commander of the Blood Knights stationed in Silvermoon City, oversees the training and assigns this trial to aspiring adepts.

faq.q: Why do adepts have to recover an insignia from a dead knight?
faq.answer: When the Blood Knights were originally established, only a limited set of official insignia were forged. Each new initiate must inherit their badge of office from a fallen veteran, in this case Blood Knight Dawnstar in Deatholme.

faq.q: Where are the Corrupted Kor Gems found?
faq.answer: They are recovered from female naga dwelling in the submerged ruins leading up to Blackfathom Deeps along the coast of Ashenvale.

faq.q: Where are the Bloodforged Ingots located?
faq.answer: The crate of Bloodforged Ingots is stashed inside the courtyard stables of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest, hidden away by Landen Stilwell.

faq.q: Where is the Blood of the Wrathful found?
faq.answer: It is taken from Zelemar the Wrathful, a dark figure residing deep within the lava caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar.

angles.text: This quest is an essential milestone for blood elf paladins, testing their mastery over the Light and granting them both their formal insignia and their iconic blood-tempered ranseur.
The trials take blood elf initiates directly through major Horde territories, requiring them to operate in Silverpine Forest, Ashenvale, and even the chasms beneath the orc capital of Orgrimmar.
The collection of Bloodforged Ingots and Corrupted Kor Gems highlights the specialized metallurgy and arcane techniques unique to the Blood Knights' armaments.
